paragraphs.html: In 1869, on the banks of the Kalamazoo River in Plainwell, Michigan, a massive four-story stone building rose to become the largest buckwheat flour mill in the country. For decades, it was the heartbeat of a small Michigan town — grinding grain, employing workers, and feeding communities across the region.

When the milling era ended, the building stood quiet. But its thick stone walls, heavy timber beams, and the spirit of honest craftsmanship endured. Today, the Old Mill is listed on the National Register of Historic Places — a testament to the people who built it and the community that preserved it.

items.text: The mill is constructed on the Kalamazoo River, becoming the largest buckwheat flour mill in the nation.
The mill era winds down as industrial milling shifts elsewhere. The building is repurposed over the decades.
The building earns its place on the National Register of Historic Places, ensuring its preservation for future generations.
The Old Mill Brewpub & Grill fills the building with the aromas of craft beer and scratch-made food, honoring its industrial heritage with warm, welcoming hospitality.

items.title: Brewed In-House
items.body: Every craft beer on our tap list is brewed right here in the mill. From session bitters to barrel-aged barleywines, we make beer the way it should be made.

items.title: Scratch Kitchen
items.body: Our kitchen team smokes meats low and slow, batters perch in our own Crazy Beaver lager, and makes everything from coleslaw to cheese dip from scratch.

items.title: Community Hub
items.body: From families to friends to first dates, the Old Mill is where Plainwell gathers. Indoor and outdoor seating, games in the tap room, and daily specials keep people coming back.

data.heading: On
data.body: Every pint is brewed in-house, right here in the mill. Our rotating lineup spans easy-drinking session ales to bold, boundary-pushing creations. We also offer bottled beer, wine, and a full liquor selection.

beers.name: Plainwell Standard
beers.description: Our flagship session ale and the beer that started it all. Drawing from the English bitter tradition, the Plainwell Standard emphasizes malt flavors balanced with floral English hops. Not particularly bitter by American standards, this copper-colored pint proves session beers don't have to sacrifice character.

beers.name: Crazy Beaver
beers.description: Don't let the name fool you — Crazy Beaver is as smooth as they come. Brewed with a generous helping of maize for a clean, light cereal grain flavor and exceptionally smooth body. Just a touch of noble Saaz hops rounds it out. Perfect for a sunny afternoon on the patio.

beers.name: Island City
beers.description: Named for Plainwell's island city heritage, this American IPA delivers everything you want from the style. A clean, bready malt backbone supports citrus and floral hop character front and center. Hop-forward and bitter, but balanced enough to stay refreshing pint after pint.

beers.name: Cold West
beers.description: The best of both worlds: all the hop character and flavor of a West Coast IPA with the crisp, clean finish of a lager. Fermented cold with lager yeast and loaded with local Michigan Chinook and Citra hops. The result is a beer that's bold on flavor but impossibly clean.

beers.name: Earth Angel
beers.description: Brewed not with a devilish name, but an angelic one. Light in color and bold in flavor, Earth Angel delivers notes of sugar cookies and honeycomb with an aroma of fresh pear, clove, meadow grass, and lilies. This beer is simply heaven on earth — and at 8.3%, it packs a divine punch.

beers.name: Sunshine
beers.description: A bold stout with layers of bittersweet chocolate and licorice, finishing with a warm hint of coffee. We incorporate substantial amounts of oatmeal in the grain bill, which contributes to an incredibly rich, silky mouthfeel that you'll feel from the first sip to the last.

beers.name: Vanilla Sunshine
beers.description: Everything you love about Sunshine, elevated with fair trade Mexican vanilla. The natural bittersweet chocolate, licorice, and coffee notes of the base stout are deepened and enhanced by that complex sweetness that only real vanilla can bring. Dessert-like without being sweet.

beers.name: BEERRH
beers.description: Our most adventurous creation — a homage to a classic French aperitif made of fortified red wine and quinine. This plummy red ale is brewed with Michigan cherries, Cabernet Sauvignon grapes, and quinine syrup (the main flavor of tonic water). Fruit-forward, herbal, and completely unlike anything else you've had.

beers.name: Little Boy Barley
beers.description: Good things take time. Little Boy Barley spends a full year aging in our cellar before it ever meets a glass. The result is rich marmalade sweetness, velvety caramel flavor, and a warming alcohol presence that's perfect as we await our spring thaw. A seasonal release meant to be savored.

beers.name: Brewer's Batch #100
beers.description: Created to commemorate brewer Adam's 100th batch at the Old Mill. This triple-hopped double New England IPA features Amarillo, Calypso, Citra, Mosaic, and Michigan-grown Chinook and Centennial hops. Prioritizes flavor over bitterness with an exceptionally prominent, juicy hop profile. A celebration in a glass.

events.desc: A Plainwell legend. Every Wednesday we roll out a massive, creative wet burrito with a new twist. Past creations have become the stuff of local lore. Get here early — they go fast.

events.name: Live Music
events.desc: We bring in local and regional talent for live music nights in the pub. Acoustic sets, full bands, and everything in between. Check our socials for the latest lineup.

events.name: Daily Specials
events.desc: We always have something special cooking. From soup of the day to the Belgian Waffle of the week, there's always a reason to stop by and see what's new.

events.name: Game Day
events.desc: Catch the big game on our TVs while you enjoy craft beers and great food. The tap room is the perfect spot to gather with friends for football, basketball, and more.

events.name: Community Gatherings

data.image_alt: Bartender pouring a craft beer at the Old Mill tap

paragraphs.html: Built in 1869, this four-story stone building on the banks of the Kalamazoo River was once the largest buckwheat flour mill in the country. Today it stands as a proud landmark, listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

We’ve honored the building’s industrial heritage while transforming it into a warm, welcoming brewpub where great craft beer meets a scratch-made kitchen. Every pint is brewed in-house, and every plate is made from fresh ingredients.
Whether you’re settling in for a family dinner, catching the game with friends, or enjoying a quiet pint on the patio overlooking the river, the Old Mill is your place.

data.heading: What We Do With
data.body: Short version: the only information we collect through this site is what you type into the job application, and it goes to our managers. Here's the longer version.

items.title: What we collect
items.body: Only what you type into a form on this site. The job application asks for your name, email, phone number, the position you want, employment type, availability, earliest start date, and whatever you write in the experience and notes boxes. We don't ask for a Social Security number, a date of birth, or bank details, and you shouldn't send them.

items.title: Where it goes
items.body: Applications are stored in LibrePublish, the content system that runs this site, and emailed to our managers at mgmt@oldmillbrew.com. Old Mill managers and the people who maintain the site are the only ones who see them. We don't sell, rent or trade what you send us.

items.title: How long we keep it
items.body: We hold on to applications while we're hiring and for a while after, in case a spot opens up. If you'd rather we delete yours, ask and we will.

items.title: Cookies and tracking
items.body: This site stores one thing in your browser: whether you chose the light or dark theme. There's no analytics, no advertising pixel and no tracking of you across other sites.

items.title: Things we load from other companies
items.body: Our web fonts come from Google, the map on the Visit page is a Google Maps embed, and the Order Online button hands you off to Toast. Those companies see the request your browser makes, including your IP address, and their own privacy policies apply once you're on their page.

items.title: Your choices
items.body: Want a copy of what you sent us, or want it deleted? Email mgmt@oldmillbrew.com or call (269) 204-6601 and tell us which. We'll take care of it.

data.heading: Questions about any of this?
data.body: Email mgmt@oldmillbrew.com, call (269) 204-6601, or stop in at 717 E. Bridge Street in Plainwell and ask for a manager. Last updated September 1, 2026.

seo.seo_description: What Old Mill Brewpub & Grill collects through this website, where it goes, and how to have it deleted.

data.address_note: Located on the banks of the Kalamazoo River in downtown Plainwell. The historic four-story stone building is hard to miss.

data.heading: Walk-In Only — No Reservations
data.body: We operate on a first-come, first-served basis. When you arrive, check in with our hostess, grab a drink, and have a seat in our tap room. Play a game or watch TV while you wait — we'll come find you when your table is ready.

items.title: Indoor Dining
items.body: Settle into the warmth of the original mill building. Exposed stone, heavy timbers, and the character of 150+ years of history surround you while you eat and drink.

items.title: Outdoor Patio
items.body: In warmer months, enjoy your meal on our patio overlooking the Kalamazoo River. There's nothing like a craft beer and the Michigan breeze.

items.title: The Tap Room
items.body: Our casual tap room is the perfect spot to wait for a table, meet friends, or just enjoy a pint. Games, TVs, and a relaxed vibe.

items.title: Family Friendly
items.body: We welcome families with a dedicated kids' menu and a welcoming atmosphere. The Old Mill is a place for everyone.

data.heading: Can't Make It
data.body: Order online for pickup and enjoy the Old Mill at home.

entries.title: Crazy Beaver
entries.body_markdown: Our lightest and most easy-drinking offering is brewed with lots of Maize for a light, cereal grain flavor and a smooth body, with just a touch of noble Saaz Hops.

seo.description: Our lightest and most easy-drinking offering is brewed with lots of Maize for a light, cereal grain flavor and a smooth body, with just a touch of noble Saaz Hops.

entries.title: Island City
entries.body_markdown: Our American-style IPA features a clean, bready malt backbone with a crisp, citrus and floral hop taste and aroma. This beer is hop-forward, bitter, and very refreshing.

seo.description: Our American-style IPA features a clean, bready malt backbone with a crisp, citrus and floral hop taste and aroma. This beer is hop-forward, bitter, and very refreshing.

entries.title: Sunshine
entries.body_markdown: Our Stout is bold from start to finish with flavors of bittersweet chocolate and licorice, finishing with a hint of coffee. Lots of Oatmeal in the mash gives this beer an incredibly rich mouthfeel.

seo.description: Our Stout is bold from start to finish with flavors of bittersweet chocolate and licorice, finishing with a hint of coffee. Lots of Oatmeal in the mash gives this beer an incredibly rich mouthfeel.

entries.title: BEERRH
entries.body_markdown: Just say ‘BEER’ – this incredible libation is an homage to a classic French aperitif made of fortified red wine and quinine, the main flavor of tonic water. Our plummy red beer was brewed with Michigan Cherries, Cabernet Sauvignon Grapes, and Quinine Syrup.

entries.title: Oktoberfest
entries.body_markdown: A lot of extra time and care went into crafting this traditional German Lager, which was cold-conditioned for two months. This beer is very easy drinking with a sweet cereal nose, a fresh malty body, and the smoothest finish around. Ein Prosit zum Oktoberfest!

seo.description: A lot of extra time and care went into crafting this traditional German Lager, which was cold-conditioned for two months. This beer is very easy drinking with a sweet cereal nose, a fresh malty body, and the smoothest finish around. Ein Prosit zum Oktoberfest!

entries.title: Pastry Case: Key Lime Cream Ale
entries.body_markdown: We've blended our classic Crazy Beaver Cream Ale w/ real Key Lime Juice & pure fair trade Mexican Vanilla to recreate our favorite diner pie from the pastry case for you pub pint glass. It is light, refreshing, and just a little tart, all w/ a beautifully sweet note of Vanilla

entries.title: Railside Red
entries.body_markdown: Red Ales are the middle way between meltier dark beers and hoppier Pale Ales. Brewed with premium Marris Otter Malt, our Irish-style Red strikes a balance with a biscuity, slightly boggy taste and a clean, moderately bitter finish.

entries.title: Impostor Schwarzbier
entries.body_markdown:
A Schwarzbier is a nearly-black lager that is light-bodied while retaining a complex character. Its bitterness comes not from its dark-roasted malt, but from a noticeable dose of spicy Continental Hops.

This beer has been in hiding for some time now, and returns for a limited time only!

seo.description: A Schwarzbier is a nearly-black lager that is light-bodied while retaining a complex character. Its bitterness comes not from its dark-roasted malt, but from a noticeable dose of spicy Continental Hops.

entries.title: Nordkapp
entries.body_markdown: Brewed with Citra and Comet hops and fermented with a strain of Norwegian yeast called Kveik that produces clean, citrusy, peachy-tasting beers, this New England IPA is extremely hoppy but not very bitter. It will bring sunshine to even your darkest of nights.

seo.description: Brewed with Citra and Comet hops and fermented with a strain of Norwegian yeast called Kveik that produces clean, citrusy, peachy-tasting beers, this New England IPA is extremely hoppy but not very bitter. It will bring sunshine to even your darkest of nights.

entries.title: Beer Jargon Pale Ale
entries.body_markdown: Brewed as a love letter to our brewer’s favorite ingredients, this “SMASH” beer (Single Malt And Single Hop) was brewed with premium British Maris Otter Pale Malt and Michigan-grown Chinook Hops – in this case, some of the last hops ever grown down the road at Hop Head Farms.
